title: introduce-state-stitcher-tfmodule-and-gpu-nodepool-subnet-affinity
author: Aisha Khatri
title_pretty: Introduce state-stitcher TF module and GPU nodepool subnet affinity
description:
Motivation: private deployments increasingly need to reorganize tfstate across VPC and tenant boundaries when customers add dedicated GPU subnets or migrate tenant networks. Existing migrations are ad-hoc, risky, and require long maintenance windows. This PR introduces a new, opt-in Terraform module (modules/state-stitcher) plus companion TF fragments for nodepool subnet affinity to enable safe, incremental state stitching and an automated migration helper script.

What this PR does (single-line overview): adds a state-stitcher TF module to perform controlled tfstate concatenation/relocation, implements tenant-scoped GPU nodepool -> subnet affinity constructs, provides an idempotent migration helper (scripts/state_migrate.sh), and documents upgrade and rollback procedures for the private installer.

Details: The state-stitcher module exposes an explicit mapping of source tfstates + resource selectors to a target consolidated state. It uses remote state read-only snapshots, verifies resource identity (name/labels/resource_id), and generates a migration plan file that the helper script uses to perform a staged import and state push. For GPU nodepools we add variables and lifecycle rules to bind nodepool resources to tenant_subnet claims so node allocation respects tenancy and AZ affinity.

Migration path: 1) Run terraform plan with modules/state-stitcher in dry-run to produce a migration plan file; 2) Run scripts/state_migrate.sh --dry-run to validate; 3) Run migration with snapshots + automatic rollback point (creates tfstate backup in a customer-specified backend or S3); 4) Smoke test using tests/e2e/private-upgrade-smoke.yaml; 5) Promote to main. The helper supports --rollback-on-failure and will attempt to revert any applied imports if downstream checks fail.

Compatibility and safety: This is opt-in (module not included by default in private-installer charts). The module is compatible with existing module inputs (vpc_id, tenant_id, remote_state_backend). Extensive validation is included: resource identity checks, label/tag assertions, and a pre-migration diff summary. We added unit tests for the module and an e2e smoke for the upgrade path.

Why this is different from previous TF refactors: Instead of just moving tfstate boundaries, this PR provides a declarative, verifiable stitching mechanism with a repeatable helper and documented rollback. It targets GPU tenancy problems specifically (nodepool drift where GPUs were scheduled to shared subnets), and introduces subnet affinity variables and taint-safe lifecycle to reduce migration blast radius.

review_conversation: Marco: Can you walk through the invariants the stitcher checks before performing imports? Aisha: The helper enumerates resource IDs from the source snapshot and checks name + tag patterns and an optional owner label; if any mismatch is found it refuses to continue unless --force is supplied and explicit allow-list is given. Nina: Please add an example showing a two-stage migrate for cross-account tfstate. Aisha: Added example.tfvars and an example in the README. Evan: CI e2e flakes on first run; looks like timing with remote state locking. Aisha: added a sleep + lock-check step in state_migrate.sh and retried CI. Marco: Recommend adding a safety backup step to push snapshots to a separate bucket before imports. Aisha: implemented backup routine and exposed backup_backend optional var. Nina: Approved after docs update. Evan: Approved after adding retry and better logging. CI: first run failed (linting on shellcheck), fixed script to satisfy shellcheck, second run all checks passed. Merge: squash and merge with a short commit message.
release_notes: Adds 'state-stitcher' Terraform module and GPU nodepool subnet affinity helpers. Includes migration helper script with dry-run and rollback support, e2e upgrade smoke tests, and documentation. Opt-in and non-breaking by default.
risk_assessment: medium - touches tfstate; mitigations: dry-run, automated snapshot backups, preflight validators, and rollback option in helper script.
notes_for_oncall: If a customer reports nodepool allocation failures after migration, check the migration plan logs in artifacts (ci/e2e-upgrade), verify tfstate backup exists in the configured backup backend, and run scripts/state_migrate.sh --rollback <plan>. For partial failures inspect logs/lock files in remote state and contact infra oncall.
testing_summary: Unit tests for selector logic (tests/unit/test_state_stitcher.tf), shellcheck and shfmt fixes for scripts, ci e2e upgrade smoke validated cluster after migration (nodes with GPUs launched into claimed subnets).
acknowledgements: Thanks to infra-team (Marco, Evan) for review and SRE for e2e environment time.
notes: This PR should be applied to release branches only after running the migration dry-run against a staging snapshot. Do not enable for customers with custom state backends unless backup_backend is configured.
